summary: The ascending chain condition extends from ideals to submodules. Closure properties explain finite modules over Noetherian rings, while stabilization of kernels proves that surjective endomorphisms are invertible.
keyPoints: A module is Noetherian exactly when every submodule is finitely generated.
Submodules, quotients, extensions, and finite direct sums preserve the Noetherian property.
Finitely generated modules over a left Noetherian ring are Noetherian and Hopfian.
Right multiplication on the left regular module proves that a left Noetherian ring is directly finite.

titleEn: Submodules of Free Modules over a PID
summary: A coordinate filtration extends the submodule theorem from finite to arbitrary rank over a PID. Successor splittings and finite support produce a basis, giving freeness of all projective modules over a PID.
keyPoints: A free module is a direct sum with finite-support coordinates, not an arbitrary product.
A well-ordered basis gives compatible splittings at successor stages and unions at limit stages.
Every submodule of a free module over a commutative PID is free, without finite-generation assumptions.
Projective modules over a PID are free; arbitrary torsion-free modules need not be free.

titleEn: Simple Modules and Maximal Left Ideals
summary: A simple module is nonzero and has no proper nonzero submodule. A nonzero element makes it a quotient of the regular module by a maximal left ideal.
keyPoints: Simple left modules are quotients by maximal left ideals.
For commutative rings, annihilators distinguish the quotients by different maximal ideals.
Simple modules over an algebraically closed Laurent polynomial ring are evaluations at nonzero scalars.

titleEn: Idempotents and Direct Summands of the Regular Module
summary: A projection of the left regular module is right multiplication by an idempotent. This distinguishes splitting of a particular inclusion from projectivity of its domain.
keyPoints: A left-linear projection is determined by its value at one.
An idempotent decomposes the regular left module into two complementary left ideals.
Finite direct-sum decompositions correspond to complete orthogonal idempotent families.
Ring-product decompositions require centrality, and projective submodules need not split their given inclusions.

titleEn: Pushouts of Abelian Groups and Modules
summary: A pushout identifies the two images of a common source. In modules it is the direct sum of the targets modulo the image of their difference.
keyPoints: The maps into a pushout agree on the common source.
The quotient of the direct sum by the difference map satisfies the universal property.
The construction needs neither a commutative ring nor injective structure maps.
Abelian-group pushouts are the special case of modules over the integers.

summary: Tensor-Hom adjunction converts projectivity of two factors into projectivity of their tensor product over a commutative ring.
keyPoints: Hom from each projective factor is exact.
Composing the two exact Hom functors identifies with Hom from the tensor product.
No finite-generation hypothesis is needed.

titleEn: Closure Properties of Flat Modules and Internal Hom
summary: Tensor associativity and direct-sum distributivity give closure properties of flat modules. The same tools show that Hom from a projective module into an injective module is injective.
keyPoints: Tensor products and arbitrary direct sums of flat modules are flat.
A kernel of a surjection from a free module to a flat module is flat by the existing exact-sequence criterion.
The internal Hom from a projective module to an injective module is injective over a commutative ring.
Arbitrary direct-product closure is not asserted.

titleEn: Nakayama's Lemma over the Jacobson Radical
summary: The determinant argument proves Nakayama over an ideal in the Jacobson radical, with the local generator criterion as a consequence.
keyPoints: For a finitely generated module equal to its ideal multiple, a determinant congruent to one annihilates the module.
If the ideal lies in the Jacobson radical, that determinant is a unit and the module vanishes.
The quotient form does not require finite generation of the submodule.
Over a local ring, generators can be detected modulo the maximal ideal.

titleEn: Torsion under Colimits and Inverse Limits
summary: Finite support and nonzero products of annihilators make colimits of torsion modules torsion over a domain. Inverse limits need not preserve torsion.
keyPoints: Direct sums and quotients preserve torsion over a commutative domain.
The quotient-of-direct-sum construction proves torsion preservation for every small colimit.
The coherent element one in the inverse limit of the prime-power cyclic groups has infinite order.

titleEn: Reading the Radical Theorem and Its Correction
summary: The general intersection-of-primes theorem already contains the nilradical case. Its existing correction supplies the separating-prime argument.
keyPoints: The radical theorem is a statement for arbitrary commutative unital rings.
The nilradical identity is its zero-ideal specialization.
Use the existing localization correction when reading the printed proof.
